items.headline: Bluefin tuna are feeding within sight of the Donegal coast for the first time in living memory
items.standfirst: A cold upwelling off the north-west shelf has pushed baitfish inshore, and the tuna have followed them into water shallow enough to see from the cliffs.

image.alt: Fishing boats moored at Killybegs harbour under low cloud

items.headline: Sussex kelp restoration enters its fifth winter with the first signs of a self-sustaining bed
items.standfirst: Trawling was excluded from 300 square kilometres in 2021. The kelp took three years to show up, and is now reproducing without help.

image.alt: Kelp fronds photographed from below in green water

items.headline: What the new North Sea allocation actually changes for a boat under twelve metres
items.standfirst: The headline figure went up. For most of the small-boat fleet, the number that matters went down.

image.alt: A small inshore fishing boat alongside a stone quay

items.headline: Sea temperature at Rockall hits an August record for the third year running
items.standfirst: The buoy has been on station since 1978. The three warmest readings in its history have all come since 2024.

image.alt: A weather buoy in heavy swell under grey sky

items.headline: Inside a herring spawning run, filmed at forty metres
items.standfirst: Three nights on the seabed with a low-light rig, waiting for a shoal that arrives without warning and leaves before dawn.

items.headline: How fishing quota actually works, in two minutes
items.standfirst: Total allowable catch, track record, leasing and the under-ten pool — drawn out on a whiteboard.

items.headline: A day recovering ghost gear off the Copeland Islands
items.standfirst: Volunteers lifted 1.4 tonnes of abandoned net in a single tide. Most of it was still fishing.

items.headline: Strangford oyster growers report the cleanest season since the 2018 closure
items.standfirst: Improved catchment management upstream has done what eight years of shellfish-water designations could not.

image.alt: Oyster trestles exposed at low water

items.headline: A seagrass planting machine built from a modified potato planter
items.standfirst: Hand-planting seagrass costs about £45 a square metre. This rig, welded together in a shed in Cornwall, does it for under six.

image.alt: A towed planting frame on the deck of a small workboat

items.headline: Shore-power grants open for harbours under 200 berths
items.standfirst: Boats running generators alongside are the largest single source of harbour-side emissions in most small ports.

image.alt: Power bollards on a harbour wall

items.headline: Blue shark tags reveal a Celtic Sea nursery nobody had mapped
items.standfirst: Sixty tags deployed over two summers show juveniles holding in one patch of water for months at a time.

image.alt: A blue shark alongside a research vessel before release

items.headline: Reading a fish's age from a bone the size of a grain of rice
items.standfirst: Otoliths lay down growth rings like a tree. Under polarised light, a decade of a cod's life becomes legible.

items.headline: Crab processor closes after forty years, and the boats have nowhere else to land
items.standfirst: The nearest alternative buyer is a hundred and ten miles by road, which is further than the margin will stretch.

image.alt: Stacked crab pots on a quayside

items.headline: Inspecting a tidal turbine in a four-knot current
items.standfirst: There is a twenty-minute window at slack water. Everything else is holding on.

items.headline: Twelve months after the sandeel closure, the seabird numbers are the first thing to move
items.standfirst: Kittiwake productivity on two monitored colonies is up sharply. Whether the closure caused it is a harder question.

image.alt: Kittiwakes nesting on a sea cliff
